milestones.label: Boot and process initialization
milestones.evidenceBoundary: Primary executable reaches the current structured stop after creating and resuming one guest thread; title entry and child workload completion are not complete

milestones.label: Logical window and message flow
milestones.evidenceBoundary: Primary logical window creation, style, DC, activation, frame-change move, already-visible ShowWindow, synchronous WM_PAINT with BeginPaint/EndPaint, and owner-thread SetTimer registration pass. Four due logical window-timer occurrences, including two after action-input consumption, are lazily materialized as low-priority WM_TIMER on an empty current-thread queue and dispatched through the same registered stdcall TIMERPROC in Node and Chrome. Replacement, KillTimer, queued pointer messages, filtered and cross-thread retrieval, and general message-flow breadth remain partial.

milestones.label: Immutable source asset access
milestones.evidenceBoundary: Primary system.arc opens through the immutable boot-archive snapshot mount and completes bounded header, index, and ipl._bp member reads while BGI.gdb stays writable profile state; remaining archives and general asset breadth are not claimed

milestones.label: First present and readable screen
milestones.evidenceBoundary: Controlled Canvas pixel passes; primary D3D9 logical device, system-memory textures, level-zero surface/GDI fill, locked vertex buffer, fixed-function state, Clear, two bounded scene/draw/present cycles, Rust-owned lazy texture backing with atomic LockRect/UnlockRect, generation-checked partial UpdateTexture publication, and synchronous Worker WebGL2 materialization are complete. The integrated action/timer profile reaches four TIMERPROC completions, two after input consumption, while preserving the 1280x720 black browser frame and reaches no third Present. Readable title content, queued action-message response, resize, device loss/recovery, general stack overflow/SEH, and long-run stability remain unproven.

milestones.label: User input consumption
milestones.evidenceBoundary: The active Node/Chrome-equivalent profile commits a primary left-button down event after semantic main-timer cycle 253, consumes GetAsyncKeyState(VK_LBUTTON) as 0xFFFF8001, commits release, and continues through two later Rust-owned WM_TIMER/TIMERPROC deliveries within the 320-cycle bound. This proves transport, consumption, release, and timer composition without a second Windows-state authority; it reaches no third Present. Visible gameplay response, queued pointer messages, DirectInput keyboard/mouse devices, and general input remain unproven.

milestones.label: Audible output
milestones.evidenceBoundary: Controlled 880 Hz browser pulse passes; primary DirectSound8 reaches an 88,200-byte zero-filled secondary sample backing through Lock/Unlock and accepts looping Play, while browser audio transport, audible primary output, and WinMM audio are not reached

milestones.label: Save, browser restart, and load
milestones.evidenceBoundary: Rust-owned writable profile and SQLite generation/idempotency/rollback foundation pass; controlled guest browser commit, restart, and load are not demonstrated
